notes: The command is registered at POS_DEAD/LVL_BUILDER (31); the separate LVL_HIGOD threshold remains in the handler (R2/R5e).
Root listing follows alphasort, the Lua filter, %-26.26s truncation, and the three-column CRLF break (R1/R2/R5e).
The mob/obj/room directory branch is selected only when arg1 begins with that prefix; the is_scripts_root name is intentionally inverted (R1/R2/R5e).
A missing or unsafe selected directory returns only Invalid lua edit option.\r\n (R1/R4/R5e).
An empty valid directory emits exactly None.\r\n (R1/R4/R5e).
A non-mob/obj/room arg becomes the root filename and ignores the original second token (R1/R2/R5e).
A subdirectory plus filename is read through the C CRLF loader (R1/R3/R5e).
Below LVL_HIGOD, an unreadable/missing target returns only Invalid lua edit option.\r\n (R1/R4/R5e).
The .lua test is strstr rather than a suffix test; a second dot then fails valid_filename without appending another suffix (R1/R2/R5e).
Levels 31-35 view raw content and do not enter CON_TEDIT; level 36 and above edit (R1/R2/R5e).
The shared general_file_edit path emits editor help, Edit file below, current CRLF content, PLR_WRITING, CON_TEDIT, and the exact room act (R1/R3/R5e).
Save strips CR bytes before writing, emits Saved.\r\n, logs the C OLC save record through slog, and matches the directly-written scratch twin byte-for-byte (R1/R4/R5e).
A subsequent editor entry reads the persisted LF file back into C's CRLF buffer (R1/R3/R5e).
luaedit passes kill_on_empty=TRUE; an empty save removes the file, emits Deleted.\r\n, and logs OLC: <name> deletes '<path>'. (R1/R4/R5e).
After deletion, edit_file follows the no-read/write path and starts an empty editor buffer (R1/R3/R5e).
A missing target is editable as an empty buffer and a non-empty save creates it under the anchored scripts root (R1/R4/R5e).
The C filename regex is preserved verbatim, including its optional wildcard byte (R1/R4/R5e).
Raw parent components are rejected before filepath cleaning; the C regex remains authoritative for filenames/directories (R2/R4/R5e).
The shared loader mirrors READ_SIZE chunking and the MAX_STRING_LENGTH failure boundary (R1/R4/R5e).
